title: Huge Database
author: vvs_nq
selftext:
Hey, im working on a new project. i already built a terminal with ai analysis which works great. problem is the ai only analyzes current data and i want to feed it now with strategies, reports, data, journals and so on.   
i got almost 1,000 files here with 1500+ pages and its still growing. i just started with this and im very excited on how far ill get. in best case scenario i can create a trading bot with this and my logic without problems but we will see. 

has anyone in here experience with this? would be cool to hear your opinion and stories

comments.author: hikewithcaramel
comments.body:
We have been running a multi-bot algorithmic setup (MULA_WANG) for over six months in an exhaustive hands-off sandbox phase, including an LLM-discretionary hybrid. Our core advice: Do not feed the AI raw strategies and expect it to trade.
AI is an exceptional analyst but a terrible executor. If you dump 1,500 pages of text into a prompt, the model will experience attention fragmentation, hallucinate mathematical boundaries, and eventually blow up an account if given direct API access.
To make this work safely:
The "AI Proposes, Code Disposes" Pattern: The AI should only output a structured decision vector (e.g., action, confidence). Your local Python code must handle all actual execution, dynamic position sizing, and risk rails.
Build a Local Database First: Vectorize your strategies and reports locally. Use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to inject only the highly relevant snippets into the LLM context.
Keep the machine on a tight leash!

replies.author: Xolo-Rey
replies.body: Learning this the hard way cost me months and money.  This is insanely invaluable advice.  AI doesn't do math.  It must call a tool or calculator or otherwise it will just make it up and there is no way to fix that....Ever.

replies.author: hikewithcaramel
replies.body: Another thing I found really useful was using Claude Sonnet and Claude code in tandem to write the code for the bots. Post build I then debugged and audited with Fable 5 for deeper reasoning

comments.author: jess-oleander
comments.body: You need a data warehouse! I would build a skill to have your agent transform the files into tabular format, upload all of those into a data warehouse, and then you can have a scheduled job do the same thing for new data daily or hourly or whatever cadence you need. I bet you'll use way less tokens analyzing the data too.

replies.body: thanks for the advice. i already made it working. just need some additional forwardtesting and then ill try it out to pass evals and get some payouts with that
